author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nashua South remained unbeaten Wednesday with a 2-1 boys soccer victory over Manchester Memorial, moving the Purple Panthers to 4-0 early in the season.

Kevin Araujo shaped both South goals. Sixteen minutes into the match, his corner kick found senior Max Friday for a header and a 1-0 lead. Manchester Memorial answered nine minutes later when Leis Taric chased down a long ball and scored in his season debut.

South regained the advantage four minutes into the second half. A clearance created a one-on-one opportunity for Araujo, who beat the defender with his speed and finished low for his first goal of the season. Memorial increased its pressure afterward, but South protected the one-goal margin through the final whistle.

South coach Tom Bellen told Manchester Ink Link that the result came despite a performance below the team’s preferred level, while Memorial coach Jerold White pointed to quicker decisions with the ball as an area to improve. The close match offered both teams an early-season test: Nashua South showed it could win without its best performance, and Memorial stayed within one play of an undefeated opponent.
dek: Kevin Araujo assisted on the opening goal and scored the winner as the Purple Panthers improved to 4-0.
headline: Nashua South boys soccer stays unbeaten with 2-1 win over Manchester Memorial
